First string\n462\t * @param {string} b - Second string\n463\t * @returns {number} The edit distance between the strings\n464\t */\n465\texport const levenshteinDistance = (a, b) => {\n466\t  const aLower = a.toLowerCase();\n467\t  const bLower = b.toLowerCase();\n468\t\n469\t  if (aLower === bLower) return 0;\n470\t  if (aLower.length === 0) return bLower.length;\n471\t  if (bLower.length === 0) return aLower.length;\n472\t\n473\t  const matrix = [];\n474\t\n475\t  for (let i = 0; i <= bLower.length; i++) {\n476\t    matrix[i] = [i];\n477\t  }\n478\t\n479\t  for (let j = 0; j <= aLower.length; j++) {\n480\t    matrix[0][j] = j;\n481\t  }\n482\t\n483\t  for (let i = 1; i <= bLower.length; i++) {\n484\t    for (let j = 1; j <= aLower.length; j++) {\n485\t      if (bLower.charAt(i - The user-provided model name\n503\t * @param {string[]} validModels - Array of valid model names\n504\t * @param {number} maxSuggestions - Maximum number of suggestions to return\n505\t * @param {number} maxDistance - Maximum Levenshtein distance to consider\n506\t * @returns {string[]} Array of suggested model names\n507\t */\n508\texport const findSimilarModels = (input, validModels, maxSuggestions = 3, maxDistance = 3) => {\n509\t  const suggestions = validModels\n510\t    .map(model => ({\n511\t      model,\n512\t      distance: levenshteinDistance(input, model),\n513\t    }))\n514\t    .filter(({ distance }) => distance <= maxDistance)\n515\t    .sort((a, b) => a.distance - getInstalledCodexModels = async () => {\n  if (!cachedInstalledCodexModelsPromise) {\n    cachedInstalledCodexModelsPromise = (async () => {\n      try {\n        const { stdout } = await [...new Set(modelSlugs)] : null;\n      } catch {\n        return null;\n      }\n    })();\n  }\n\n  return cachedInstalledCodexModelsPromise;\n};\n\nexport const resolveRuntimeDefaultModel = async (tool, options = {}) => {\n  const toolName = (tool || 'claude').toString().toLowerCase();\n  const preferredDefault = defaultModels[toolName] || defaultModels.claude;\n\n  if (toolName !== 'codex') {\n    return preferredDefault;\n  }\n\n  const availableCodexModels = options.availableCodexModels === undefined ? await getInstalledCodexModels() : options.availableCodexModels;\n\n  if (!Array.isArray(availableCodexModels) || availableCodexModels.length === 0) {\n    return preferredDefault;\n  }\n\n  if (availableCodexModels.includes(preferredDefault)) {\n    return preferredDefault;\n  }\n\n  return CODEX_DEFAULT_FALLBACK_CHAIN.find(model => availableCodexModels.includes(model)) || preferredDefault;\n};\n\n/**\n * Map model name to full model ID for a specific tool\n * @param {string} tool - The tool name (claude, agent, opencode, codex)\n * @param {string} model - The model name or alias\n * @returns {boolean} True if the model is compatible with the tool\n */\nexport const isModelCompatibleWithTool = (tool, model) => {\n  const mappedModel = mapModelForTool(tool, model);\n\n  switch (tool) {\n    case 'claude':\n      return mappedModel.startsWith('claude-') || mappedModel === 'opusplan';\n    case 'agent':\n      return mappedModel.includes('/') || Object.keys(agentModels).includes(model);\n    case 'opencode':\n      return mappedModel.includes('/') || Object.keys(opencodeModels).includes(model);\n    case 'codex':\n      return Object.keys(codexModels).includes(model) || mappedModel.startsWith('gpt-');\n    default:\n      return true;\n  }\n};\n\n/**\n * Get a list of valid model names for a tool\n * @param {string} tool - The tool name\n * @returns {string[]} Array of valid model names\n */\nexport const getValidModelsForTool = tool => {\n  switch (tool) {\n    case 'claude':\n      return Object.keys(claudeModels);\n    case 'agent':\n      return Object.keys(agentModels);\n    case 'opencode':\n      return Object.keys(opencodeModels);\n    case 'codex':\n      return Object.keys(codexModels);\n    default:\n      return [];\n  }\n};\n\n// Primary (non-alias, non-deprecated) short names shown in CLI help descriptions\n// These are the recommended model names users should see in --model help text\nexport const primaryModelNames = {\n  claude: ['opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku', 'opusplan'],\n  opencode: ['grok', 'gpt4o'],\n  codex: ['gpt-5.5', 'gpt-5.4', 'gpt-5.4-mini', 'gpt-5.3-codex', 'gpt-5.3-codex-spark'],\n  agent: ['nemotron-3-super-free', 'minimax-m2.5-free', 'big-pickle', 'gpt-5-nano', 'glm-5-free', 'deepseek-r1-free'],\n};\n\n/**\n * Build the --model CLI option description string dynamically from centralized model data.\n * @returns {string} Description like \"Model to use (for claude: opus, sonnet, ...; for agent: ...)\"\n */\nexport const buildModelOptionDescription = () => {\n  const parts = Object.entries(primaryModelNames).map(([tool, names]) => `for ${tool}: ${names.join(', ')}`);\n  return `Model to use (${parts.join('; ')})`;\n};\n\n/**\n * Get the primary choices for Claude model selection (used in review.mjs and task.mjs).\n * Returns short aliases plus key full model IDs for backward compatibility.\n * @returns {string[]}\n */\nexport const getClaudeModelChoices = () => {\n  return Object.keys(claudeModels);\n};\n\n/**\n * Validate tool-model compatibility and throw descriptive error if invalid\n * @param {string} tool - The tool name\n * @param {string} model - The model name\n * @throws {Error} If the model is not compatible with the tool\n */\nexport const validateToolModelCompatibility = (tool, model) => {\n  if (!isModelCompatibleWithTool(tool, model)) {\n    const validModels = getValidModelsForTool(tool);\n    const mappedModel = mapModelForTool(tool, model);\n\n    throw new Error(`Model '${model}' (mapped to '${mappedModel}') is not compatible with --tool ${tool}.\\n` + `Valid models for ${tool}: ${validModels.join(', ')}\\n` + 'Hint: Different tools use different model APIs and naming conventions.');\n  }\n};\n\n// ─── MODEL VALIDATION FUNCTIONS ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/**\n * Get the model map for a given tool (validation-extended version with full ID entries)\n * @param {string} tool - The tool name ('claude', 'opencode', 'codex', 'agent')\n * @returns {Object} The model mapping for the tool\n */\nconst getValidationModelMapForTool = tool => {\n  switch (tool) {\n    case 'opencode':\n      return OPENCODE_MODELS;\n    case 'codex':\n      return CODEX_MODELS;\n    case 'agent':\n      return AGENT_MODELS;\n    case 'claude':\n    default:\n      return CLAUDE_MODELS;\n  }\n};\n\n/**\n * Get the list of available model names for a tool (for display in help/error messages)\n * @param {string} tool - The tool name ('claude', 'opencode', 'codex', 'agent')\n * @returns {string[]} Array of available model short names\n */\nexport const getAvailableModelNames = tool => {\n  const modelMap = getValidationModelMapForTool(tool);\n  // Get unique short names (aliases) - exclude full model IDs that contain '/' or long claude- prefixed IDs\n  const aliases = Object.keys(modelMap).filter(key => {\n    // Keep short aliases only - exclude:\n    // - Full model IDs with slashes (e.g., 'openai/gpt-4')\n    // - Long claude-prefixed model IDs (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929')\n    // - Full gpt- prefixed IDs that are ONLY version numbers (e.g., 'gpt-4', 'gpt-4o', 'gpt-5')\n    // But keep descriptive aliases like 'gpt-5-nano', 'gpt-5.3-codex', 'o3-mini', 'gpt5', etc.\n    // Issue #1185: Updated regex to not filter out gpt-5-nano (a valid short alias)\n    if (key.includes('/')) return false;\n    if (key.match(/^claude-.*-\\d{8}$/)) return false; // Full claude model IDs with date\n    if (key.match(/^gpt-\\d+[a-z]?$/)) return false; // Full gpt-N or gpt-No model IDs only (e.g., gpt-4, gpt-4o, gpt-5)\n    return true;\n  });\n  return [...new Set(aliases)];\n};\n\n/**\n * Calculate Levenshtein distance between two strings (case-insensitive)\n * @param {string} a - First string\n * @param {string} b - Second string\n * @returns {number} The edit distance between the strings\n */\nexport const levenshteinDistance = (a, b) => {\n  const aLower = a.toLowerCase();\n  const bLower = b.toLowerCase();\n\n  if (aLower === bLower) return 0;\n  if (aLower.length === 0) return bLower.length;\n  if (bLower.length === 0) return aLower.length;\n\n  const matrix = [];\n\n  for (let i = 0; i <= bLower.length; i++) {\n    matrix[i] = [i];\n  }\n\n  for (let j = 0; j <= aLower.length; j++) {\n    matrix[0][j] = j;\n  }\n\n  for (let i = 1; i <= bLower.length; i++) {\n    for (let j = 1; j <= aLower.length; j++) {\n      if (bLower.charAt(i - 1) === aLower.charAt(j - 1)) {\n        matrix[i][j] = matrix[i - 1][j - 1];\n      } else {\n        matrix[i][j] = Math.min(\n          matrix[i - 1][j - 1] + 1, // substitution\n          matrix[i][j - 1] + 1, // insertion\n          matrix[i - 1][j] + 1 // deletion\n        );\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  return matrix[bLower.length][aLower.length];\n};\n\n/**\n * Find the closest matching model names using fuzzy matching\n * @param {string} input - The user-provided model name\n * @param {string[]} validModels - Array of valid model names\n * @param {number} maxSuggestions - Maximum number of suggestions to return\n * @param {number} maxDistance - Maximum Levenshtein distance to consider\n * @returns {string[]} Array of suggested model names\n */\nexport const findSimilarModels = (input, validModels, maxSuggestions = 3, maxDistance = 3) => {\n  const suggestions = validModels\n    .map(model => ({\n      model,\n      distance: levenshteinDistance(input, model),\n    }))\n    .filter(({ distance }) => distance <= maxDistance)\n    .sort((a, b) => a.distance - b.distance)\n    .slice(0, maxSuggestions)\n    .map(({ model }) => model);\n\n  return suggestions;\n};\n\n/**\n * Parse model name to extract base model and optional [1m] suffix\n * @param {string} model - The model name (e.g., \"opus[1m]\", \"claude-opus-4-6[1m]\")\n * @returns {{ baseModel: string, has1mSuffix: boolean }}\n */\nexport const parseModelWith1mSuffix = model => {\n  if (!model || typeof model !== 'string') {\n    return { baseModel: model, has1mSuffix: false };\n  }\n\n  const match = model.match(/^(.+?)\\[1m\\]$/i);\n  if (match) {\n    return { baseModel: match[1], has1mSuffix: true };\n  }\n\n  return { baseModel: model, has1mSuffix: false };\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if a model supports the [1m] context window\n * @param {string} model - The base model name (without [1m] suffix)\n * @param {string} tool - The tool name\n * @returns {boolean} True if the model supports 1M context\n */\nexport const supports1mContext = (model, tool = 'claude') => {\n  if (tool !== 'claude') {\n    return false;\n  }\n\n  const normalizedModel = model.toLowerCase();\n\n  for (const supportedModel of MODELS_SUPPORTING_1M_CONTEXT) {\n    if (supportedModel.toLowerCase() === normalizedModel) {\n      return true;\n    }\n  }\n\n  const modelMap = getValidationModelMapForTool(tool);\n  const matchedKey = Object.keys(modelMap).find(key => key.toLowerCase() === normalizedModel);\n  if (matchedKey) {\n    const mappedModel = modelMap[matchedKey];\n    for (const supportedModel of MODELS_SUPPORTING_1M_CONTEXT) {\n      if (supportedModel.toLowerCase() === mappedModel.toLowerCase()) {\n        return true;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  return false;\n};\n\n/**\n * Validate a model name against the available models for a tool\n * Supports [1m] suffix for 1 million token context (Issue #1221)\n * @param {string} model - The model name to validate (e.g., \"opus\", \"opus[1m]\", \"claude-opus-4-6[1m]\")\n * @param {string} tool - The tool name ('claude', 'opencode', 'codex')\n * @returns {{ valid: boolean, message?: string, suggestions?: string[], mappedModel?: string, has1mSuffix?: boolean }}\n */\nexport const validateModelName = (model, tool = 'claude') => {\n  if (!model || typeof model !== 'string') {\n    return {\n      valid: false,\n      message: 'Model name is required',\n      suggestions: [],\n    };\n  }\n\n  const { baseModel, has1mSuffix } = parseModelWith1mSuffix(model);\n\n  const modelMap = getValidationModelMapForTool(tool);\n  const availableNames = Object.keys(modelMap);\n\n  const normalizedModel = baseModel.toLowerCase();\n  const matchedKey = availableNames.find(key => key.toLowerCase() === normalizedModel);\n\n  if (matchedKey) {\n    const mappedModel = modelMap[matchedKey];\n\n    if (has1mSuffix) {\n      if (!supports1mContext(baseModel, tool)) {\n        const supportedModels = MODELS_SUPPORTING_1M_CONTEXT.filter(m => !m.includes('-')).join(', ');\n        return {\n          valid: false,\n          message: `Model \"${baseModel}\" does not support [1m] context window.\\n   Models supporting 1M context: ${supportedModels}`,\n          suggestions: [],\n        };\n      }\n      return {\n        valid: true,\n        mappedModel: `${mappedModel}[1m]`,\n        has1mSuffix: true,\n      };\n    }\n\n    return {\n      valid: true,\n      mappedModel,\n      has1mSuffix: false,\n    };\n  }\n\n  // Model not found - [2026-04-28T13:21:57.839Z] [INFO]         "content": "> ## Documentation Index\n> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt\n> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.\n\n# Model configuration\n\n> Learn about the Claude Code model configuration, including model aliases like `opusplan`\n\n## Available models\n\nFor the `model` setting in Claude Code, you can configure either:\n\n* A **model alias**\n* A **model name**\n  * Anthropic API: A full **[model name](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview)**\n  * Bedrock: an inference profile ARN\n  * Foundry: a deployment name\n  * Vertex: a version name\n\n### Model aliases\n\nModel aliases provide a convenient way to select model settings without\nremembering exact version numbers:\n\n| Model alias      | Behavior                                                                                                                                                             |\n| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **`default`**    | Special value that clears any model override and reverts to the recommended model for your account type. Not itself a model alias                                    |\n| **`best`**       | Uses the most capable available model, currently equivalent to `opus`                                                                                                |\n| **`sonnet`**     | Uses the latest Sonnet model for daily coding tasks                                                                                                                  |\n| **`opus`**       | Uses the latest Opus model for complex reasoning tasks                                                                                                               |\n| **`haiku`**      | Uses the fast and efficient Haiku model for simple tasks                                                                                                             |\n| **`sonnet[1m]`** | Uses Sonnet with a [1 million token context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows#1m-token-context-window) for long sessions |\n| **`opus[1m]`**   | Uses Opus with a [1 million token context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows#1m-token-context-window) for long sessions   |\n| **`opusplan`**   | Special mode that uses `opus` during plan mode, then switches to `sonnet` for execution                                                                              |\n\nOn the Anthropic API, `opus` resolves to Opus 4.7 and `sonnet` resolves to Sonnet 4.6. On Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, `opus` resolves to Opus 4.6 and `sonnet` resolves to Sonnet 4.5; newer models are available on those providers by selecting the full model name explicitly or setting `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` or `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`.\n\nAliases point to the recommended version for your provider and update over time. To pin to a specific version, use the full model name (for example, `claude-opus-4-7`) or set the corresponding environment variable like `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`.\n\n<Note>\n  Opus 4.7 requires Claude Code v2.1.111 or later. Run `claude update` to upgrade.\n</Note>\n\n### Setting your model\n\nYou can configure your model in several ways, listed in order of priority:\n\n1. **During session** - Use `/model <alias|name>` to switch immediately, or run `/model` with no argument to open the picker. The picker asks for confirmation when the conversation has prior output, since the next response re-reads the full history without cached context\n2. **At startup** - Launch with `claude --model <alias|name>`\n3. **Environment variable** - Set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=<alias|name>`\n4. **Settings** - Configure permanently in your settings file using the `model`\n   field.\n\nYour `/model` selection is saved to user settings and persists across restarts. As of v2.1.117, if the project's `.claude/settings.json` pins a different model, Claude Code also writes your choice to `.claude/settings.local.json` so it continues to apply in that project after a restart. Managed settings take precedence and reapply on the next launch.\n\nWhen the active model at startup comes from project or managed settings rather than your own selection, the startup header shows which settings file set it. Run `/model` to override for the current session.\n\nExample usage:\n\n```bash theme={null}\n# Start with Opus\nclaude --model opus\n\n# Switch to Sonnet during session\n/model sonnet\n```\n\nExample settings file:\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n    \"permissions\": {\n        ...\n    },\n    \"model\": \"opus\"\n}\n```\n\n## Restrict model selection\n\nEnterprise administrators can use `availableModels` in [managed or policy settings](/en/settings#settings-files) to restrict which models users can select.\n\nWhen `availableModels` is set, users cannot switch to models not in the list via `/model`, `--model` flag, or `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` environment variable.\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"availableModels\": [\"sonnet\", \"haiku\"]\n}\n```\n\n### Default model behavior\n\nThe Default option in the model picker is not affected by `availableModels`. It always remains available and represents the system's runtime default [based on the user's subscription tier](#default-model-setting).\n\nEven with `availableModels: []`, users can still use Claude Code with the Default model for their tier.\n\n### Control the model users run on\n\nThe `model` setting is an initial selection, not enforcement. It sets which model is active when a session starts, but users can still open `/model` and pick Default, which resolves to the system default for their tier regardless of what `model` is set to.\n\nTo fully control the model experience, combine three settings:\n\n* **`availableModels`**: restricts which named models users can switch to\n* **`model`**: sets the initial model selection when a session starts\n* **`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`** / **`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`** / **`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`**: control what the Default option and the `sonnet`, `opus`, and `haiku` aliases resolve to\n\nThis example starts users on Sonnet 4.5, limits the picker to Sonnet and Haiku, and pins Default to resolve to Sonnet 4.5 rather than the latest release:\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"model\": \"claude-sonnet-4-5\",\n  \"availableModels\": [\"claude-sonnet-4-5\", \"haiku\"],\n  \"env\": {\n    \"ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL\": \"claude-sonnet-4-5\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nWithout the `env` block, a user who selects Default in the picker would get the latest Sonnet release, bypassing the version pin in `model` and `availableModels`.\n\n### Merge behavior\n\nWhen `availableModels` is set at multiple levels, such as user settings and project settings, arrays are merged and deduplicated. To enforce a strict allowlist, set `availableModels` in managed or policy settings which take highest priority.\n\n### Mantle model IDs\n\nWhen the [Bedrock Mantle endpoint](/en/amazon-bedrock#use-the-mantle-endpoint) is enabled, entries in `availableModels` that start with `anthropic.` are added to the `/model` picker as custom options and routed to the Mantle endpoint. This is an exception to the alias-only matching described in [Pin models for third-party deployments](#pin-models-for-third-party-deployments). The setting still restricts the picker to listed entries, so include the standard aliases alongside any Mantle IDs.\n\n## Special model behavior\n\n### `default` model setting\n\nThe behavior of `default` depends on your account type:\n\n* **Max and Team Premium**: defaults to Opus 4.7\n* **Pro, Team Standard, Enterprise, and Anthropic API**: defaults to Sonnet 4.6\n* **Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry**: defaults to Sonnet 4.5\n\nClaude Code may automatically fall back to Sonnet if you hit a usage threshold with Opus.\n\n<Note>\n  On April 23, 2026, the default model for Enterprise pay-as-you-go and Anthropic API users will change to Opus 4.7. To keep a different default, set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or the `model` field in [server-managed settings](/en/server-managed-settings).\n</Note>\n\n### `opusplan` model setting\n\nThe `opusplan` model alias provides an automated hybrid approach:\n\n* **In plan mode** - Uses `opus` for complex reasoning and architecture\n  decisions\n* **In execution mode** - Automatically switches to `sonnet` for code generation\n  and implementation\n\nThis gives you the best of both worlds: Opus's superior reasoning for planning,\nand Sonnet's efficiency for execution.\n\nThe plan-mode Opus phase runs with the standard 200K context window. The automatic 1M upgrade described in [Extended context](#extended-context) applies to the `opus` model setting and does not extend to `opusplan`.\n\n### Adjust effort level\n\n[Effort levels](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort) control adaptive reasoning, which lets the model decide whether and how much to think on each step based on task complexity. Lower effort is faster and cheaper for straightforward tasks, while higher effort provides deeper reasoning for complex problems.\n\nEffort is supported on Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6. The available levels depend on the model:\n\n| Model                   | Levels                                  |\n| :---------------------- | :-------------------------------------- |\n| Opus 4.7                | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` |\n| Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`          |\n\nIf you set a level the active model does not support, Claude Code falls back to the highest supported level at or below the one you set. For example, `xhigh` runs as `high` on Opus 4.6.\n\nAs of v2.1.117, the default effort is `xhigh` on Opus 4.7 and `high` on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6.\n\nWhen you first run Opus 4.7, Claude Code applies `xhigh` even if you previously set a different effort level for Opus 4.6 or Sonnet 4.6. Run `/effort` again to choose a different level after switching.\n\n`low`, `medium`, `high`, and `xhigh` persist across sessions. `max` provides the deepest reasoning with no constraint on token spending and applies to the current session only, except when set through the `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` environment variable.\n\n#### Choose an effort level\n\nEach level trades token spend against capability. The default suits most coding tasks; adjust when you want a different balance.\n\n| Level    | When to use it                                                                                                                         |\n| :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `low`    | Reserve for short, scoped, latency-sensitive tasks that are not intelligence-sensitive                                                 |\n| `medium` | Reduces token usage for cost-sensitive work that can trade off some intelligence                                                       |\n| `high`   | Balances token usage and intelligence. Use as a minimum for intelligence-sensitive work, or to reduce token spend relative to `xhigh`  |\n| `xhigh`  | Best results for most coding and agentic tasks. Recommended default on Opus 4.7                                                        |\n| `max`    | Can improve performance on demanding tasks but may show diminishing returns and is prone to overthinking. Test before adopting broadly |\n\nThe effort scale is calibrated per model, so the same level name does not represent the same underlying value across models.\n\nFor one-off deep reasoning without changing your session setting, include \"ultrathink\" in your prompt. This adds an in-context instruction telling the model to reason more on that turn; it does not change the effort level sent to the API.\n\n#### Set the effort level\n\nYou can change effort through any of the following:\n\n* **`/effort`**: run `/effort` with no arguments to open an interactive slider, `/effort` followed by a level name to set it directly, or `/effort auto` to reset to the model default\n* **In `/model`**: use left/right arrow keys to adjust the effort slider when selecting a model\n* **`--effort` flag**: pass a level name to set it for a single session when launching Claude Code\n* **Environment variable**: set `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` to a level name or `auto`\n* **Settings**: set `effortLevel` in your settings file\n* **Skill and subagent frontmatter**: set `effort` in a [skill](/en/skills#frontmatter-reference) or [subagent](/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields) markdown file to override the effort level when that skill or subagent runs\n\nThe environment variable takes precedence over all other methods, then your configured level, then the model default. Frontmatter effort applies when that skill or subagent is active, overriding the session level but not the environment variable.\n\nThe effort slider appears in `/model` when a supported model is selected. The current effort level is also displayed next to the logo and spinner, for example \"with low effort\", so you can confirm which setting is active without opening `/model`.\n\n#### Adaptive reasoning and fixed thinking budgets\n\nAdaptive reasoning makes thinking optional on each step, so Claude can respond faster to routine prompts and reserve deeper thinking for steps that benefit from it. If you want Claude to think more or less often than the current level produces, you can say so directly in your prompt or in `CLAUDE.md`; the model responds to that guidance within its effort setting.\n\nOpus 4.7 always uses adaptive reasoning. The fixed thinking budget mode and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING` do not apply to it.\n\nOn Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, you can set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1` to revert to the previous fixed thinking budget controlled by `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`. See [environment variables](/en/env-vars).\n\n### Extended context\n\nOpus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6 support a [1 million token context window](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows#1m-token-context-window) for long sessions with large codebases.\n\nAvailability varies by model and plan. On Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, Opus is automatically upgraded to 1M context with no additional configuration. This applies to both Team Standard and Team Premium seats.\n\n| Plan                      | Opus with 1M context                                                                                      | Sonnet with 1M context                                                                                    |\n| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Max, Team, and Enterprise | Included with subscription                                                                                | Requires [extra usage](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-extra-usage-for-paid-claude-plans) |\n| Pro                       | Requires [extra usage](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-extra-usage-for-paid-claude-plans) | Requires [extra usage](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12429409-extra-usage-for-paid-claude-plans) |\n| API and pay-as-you-go     | Full access                                                                                               | Full access                                                                                               |\n\nTo disable 1M context entirely, set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1`. This removes 1M model variants from the model picker. See [environment variables](/en/env-vars).\n\nThe 1M context window uses standard model pricing with no premium for tokens beyond 200K. For plans where extended context is included with your subscription, usage remains covered by your subscription. For plans that access extended context through extra usage, tokens are billed to extra usage.\n\nIf your account supports 1M context, the option appears in the model picker (`/model`) in the latest versions of Claude Code. If you don't see it, try restarting your session.\n\nYou can also use the `[1m]` suffix with model aliases or full model names:\n\n```bash theme={null}\n# Use the opus[1m] or sonnet[1m] alias\n/model opus[1m]\n/model sonnet[1m]\n\n# Or append [1m] to a full model name\n/model claude-opus-4-7[1m]\n```\n\n## Checking your current model\n\nYou can see which model you're currently using in several ways:\n\n1. In [status line](/en/statusline) (if configured)\n2. In `/status`, which also displays your account information.\n\n## Add a custom model option\n\nUse `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION` to add a single custom entry to the `/model` picker without replacing the built-in aliases. This is useful for LLM gateway deployments or testing model IDs that Claude Code does not list by default.\n\nThis example sets all three variables to make a gateway-routed Opus deployment selectable:\n\n```bash theme={null}\nexport ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION=\"my-gateway/claude-opus-4-7\"\nexport ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_NAME=\"Opus via Gateway\"\nexport ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_DESCRIPTION=\"Custom deployment routed through the internal LLM gateway\"\n```\n\nThe custom entry appears at the bottom of the `/model` picker. `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_NAME` and `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION_DESCRIPTION` are optional. If omitted, the model ID is used as the name and the description defaults to `Custom model (<model-id>)`.\n\nClaude Code skips validation for the model ID set in `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION`, so you can use any string your API endpoint accepts.\n\n## Environment variables\n\nYou can use the following environment variables, which must be full **model\nnames** (or equivalent for your API provider), to control the model names that the aliases map to.\n\n| Environment variable             | Description                                                                                   |\n| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`   | The model to use for `opus`, or for `opusplan` when Plan Mode is active.                      |\n| `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` | The model to use for `sonnet`, or for `opusplan` when Plan Mode is not active.                |\n| `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`  | The model to use for `haiku`, or [background functionality](/en/costs#background-token-usage) |\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`     | The model to use for [subagents](/en/sub-agents)                                              |\n\nNote: `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` is deprecated in favor of\n`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`.\n\n### Pin models for third-party deployments\n\nWhen deploying Claude Code through [Bedrock](/en/amazon-bedrock), [Vertex AI](/en/google-vertex-ai), or [Foundry](/en/microsoft-foundry), pin model versions before rolling out to users.\n\nWithout pinning, Claude Code uses model aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`) that resolve to the latest version. When Anthropic releases a new model that isn't yet enabled in a user's account, Bedrock and Vertex AI users see a notice and fall back to the previous version for that session, while Foundry users see errors because Foundry has no equivalent startup check.\n\n<Warning>\n  Set all three model environment variables to specific version IDs as part of your initial setup. Pinning lets you control when your users move to a new model.\n</Warning>\n\nUse the following environment variables with version-specific model IDs for your provider:\n\n| Provider  | Example                                                              |\n| :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Bedrock   | `export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL='us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7'` |\n| Vertex AI | `export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL='claude-opus-4-7'`              |\n| Foundry   | `export ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL='claude-opus-4-7'`              |\n\nApply the same pattern for `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` and `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`. For current and legacy model IDs across all providers, see [Models overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview). To upgrade users to a new model version, update these environment variables and redeploy.\n\nTo enable [extended context](#extended-context) for a pinned model, append `[1m]` to the model ID in `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` or `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`:\n\n```bash theme={null}\nexport ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL='claude-opus-4-7[1m]'\n```\n\nThe `[1m]` suffix applies the 1M context window to all usage of that alias, including `opusplan`. Claude Code strips the suffix before sending the model ID to your provider. Only append `[1m]` when the underlying model supports 1M context, such as Opus 4.7 or Sonnet 4.6.\n\n<Note>\n  The `settings.availableModels` allowlist still applies when using third-party providers. Filtering matches on the model alias (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`), not the provider-specific model ID.\n</Note>\n\n### Customize pinned model display and capabilities\n\nWhen you pin a model on a third-party provider, the provider-specific ID appears as-is in the `/model` picker and Claude Code may not recognize which features the model supports. You can override the display name and declare capabilities with companion environment variables for each pinned model.\n\nThese variables take effect on third-party providers such as Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Foundry. The `_NAME` and `_DESCRIPTION` variables also take effect when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points to an [LLM gateway](/en/llm-gateway). They have no effect when connecting directly to `api.anthropic.com`.\n\n| Environment variable                                  | Description                                                                                                        |\n| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_NAME`                   | Display name for the pinned Opus model in the `/model` picker. Defaults to the model ID when not set               |\n| `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_DESCRIPTION`            | Display description for the pinned Opus model in the `/model` picker. Defaults to `Custom Opus model` when not set |\n| `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` | Comma-separated list of capabilities the pinned Opus model supports                                                |\n\nThe same `_NAME`, `_DESCRIPTION`, and `_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` suffixes are available for `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL`, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`, and `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION`.\n\nClaude Code enables features like [effort levels](#adjust-effort-level) and [extended thinking](/en/common-workflows#use-extended-thinking-thinking-mode) by matching the model ID against known patterns. Provider-specific IDs such as Bedrock ARNs or custom deployment names often don't match these patterns, leaving supported features disabled. Set `_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` to tell Claude Code which features the model actually supports:\n\n| Capability value       | Enables                                                                         |\n| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `effort`               | [Effort levels](#adjust-effort-level) and the `/effort` command                 |\n| `xhigh_effort`         | {/* min-version: 2.1.111 */}The `xhigh` effort level                            |\n| `max_effort`           | The `max` effort level                                                          |\n| `thinking`             | [Extended thinking](/en/common-workflows#use-extended-thinking-thinking-mode)   |\n| `adaptive_thinking`    | Adaptive reasoning that dynamically allocates thinking based on task complexity |\n| `interleaved_thinking` | Thinking between tool calls                                                     |\n\nWhen `_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` is set, listed capabilities are enabled and unlisted capabilities are disabled for the matching pinned model. When the variable is unset, Claude Code falls back to built-in detection based on the model ID.\n\nThis example pins Opus to a Bedrock custom model ARN, sets a friendly name, and declares its capabilities:\n\n```bash theme={null}\nexport ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL='arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:123456789012:custom-model/abc'\nexport ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_NAME='Opus via Bedrock'\nexport ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_DESCRIPTION='Opus 4.7 routed through a Bedrock custom endpoint'\nexport ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES='effort,xhigh_effort,max_effort,thinking,adaptive_thinking,interleaved_thinking'\n```\n\n### Override model IDs per version\n\nThe family-level environment variables above configure one model ID per family alias. If you need to map several versions within the same family to distinct provider IDs, use the `modelOverrides` setting instead.\n\n`modelOverrides` maps individual Anthropic model IDs to the provider-specific strings that Claude Code sends to your provider's API. When a user selects a mapped model in the `/model` picker, Claude Code uses your configured value instead of the built-in default.\n\nThis lets enterprise administrators route each model version to a specific Bedrock inference profile ARN, Vertex AI version name, or Foundry deployment name for governance, cost allocation, or regional routing.\n\nSet `modelOverrides` in your [settings file](/en/settings#settings-files):\n\n```json theme={null}\n{\n  \"modelOverrides\": {\n    \"claude-opus-4-7\": \"arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-2:123456789012:application-inference-profile/opus-prod\",\n    \"claude-opus-4-6\": \"arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-2:123456789012:application-inference-profile/opus-46-prod\",\n    \"claude-sonnet-4-6\": \"arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-2:123456789012:application-inference-profile/sonnet-prod\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\nKeys must be Anthropic model IDs as listed in the [Models overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview). For dated model IDs, include the date suffix exactly as it appears there. Unknown keys are ignored.\n\nOverrides replace the built-in model IDs that back each entry in the `/model` picker. On Bedrock, overrides take precedence over any inference profiles that Claude Code discovers automatically at startup. Values you supply directly through `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, `--model`, or the `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` environment variables are passed to the provider as-is and are not transformed by `modelOverrides`.\n\n`modelOverrides` works alongside `availableModels`. The allowlist is evaluated against the Anthropic model ID, not the override value, so an entry like `\"opus\"` in `availableModels` continues to match even when Opus versions are mapped to ARNs.\n\n### Prompt caching configuration\n\nClaude Code automatically uses [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) to optimize performance and reduce costs. You can disable prompt caching globally or for specific model tiers:\n\n| Environment variable            | Description                                                                                    |\n| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING`        | Set to `1` to disable prompt caching for all models (takes precedence over per-model settings) |\n| `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU`  | Set to `1` to disable prompt caching for Haiku models only                                     |\n| `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_SONNET` | Set to `1` to disable prompt caching for Sonnet models only                                    |\n| `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_OPUS`   | Set to `1` to disable prompt caching for Opus models only                                      |\n\nThese environment variables give you fine-grained control over prompt caching behavior. The global `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING` setting takes precedence over the model-specific settings, allowing you to quickly disable all caching when needed. The per-model settings are useful for selective control, such as when debugging specific models or working with cloud providers that may have different caching implementations.\n"

config = yargsInstance\n    .usage('Usage: solve.mjs <issue-url> [options]')\n    .command('$0 <issue-url>', 'Solve a GitHub issue or pull request', yargs => {\n      yargs.positional('issue-url', {\n        type: 'string',\n        description: 'The GitHub issue URL to solve',\n      });\n    })\n    .fail((msg, err) => {\n      // Custom fail handler to suppress yargs error output\n      // Errors will be handled in the parseArguments catch block\n      if (err) throw err; // Rethrow actual errors\n      // For validation errors, throw a clean error object with the message\n      const error = new Error(msg);\n      error.name = 'YargsValidationError';\n      throw error;\n    });\n\n  // Register all options from the definitions map\n  for (const [name, def] of Object.entries(SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS)) {\n    config = config.option(name, def);\n  }\n\n  // 'model' has a dynamic default function, so it's defined inline (not in SOLVE_OPTION_DEFINITIONS)\n  config = config\n    .option('model', {\n      type: 'string',\n      description: buildModelOptionDescription(),\n      alias: ['m', 'worker-model'],\n      default: currentParsedArgs => {\n        // Dynamic default based on tool selection (Issue #1473: centralized in models/index.mjs)\n        return defaultModels[currentParsedArgs?.tool] || defaultModels.claude;\n      },\n    })\n    .parserConfiguration({\n      'boolean-negation': true,\n    })\n    // Use yargs built-in strict mode to reject unrecognized options\n    // This prevents issues like #453 and #482 where unknown options are silently ignored\n    .strict()\n    .help('h')\n    .alias('h', 'help');\n\n  return config;\n};\n\n// Parse command line arguments - now needs yargs and hideBin passed in\nexport const parseArguments = async (yargs, hideBin) => {\n  const rawArgs = hideBin(process.argv);\n\n  // Issue #1092: Detect malformed flag patterns BEFORE yargs parsing\n  // This catches cases like \"-- model\" which yargs silently treats as positional arguments\n  const malformedResult = detectMalformedFlags(rawArgs);\n  if (malformedResult.malformed.length > 0) {\n    const error = new Error(malformedResult.errors.join('\\n'));\n    error.name = 'MalformedArgumentError';\n    throw error;\n  }\n\n  // Use .parse() instead of .argv to ensure .strict() mode works correctly\n  // When you call yargs(args) and use .argv, strict mode doesn't trigger\n  // See: https://github.com/yargs/yargs/issues - .strict() only works with .parse()\n\n  let argv;\n  let yargsInstance;\n  try {\n    // Suppress stderr output from yargs during parsing to prevent validation errors from appearing\n    // This prevents \"YError: Not enough arguments\" from polluting stderr (issue #583)\n    // Save the original stderr.write\n    const originalStderrWrite = process.stderr.write;\n    const stderrBuffer = [];\n\n    // Temporarily override stderr.write to capture output\n    process.stderr.write = function (chunk, encoding, callback) {\n      stderrBuffer.push(chunk.toString());\n      // Call the callback if provided (for compatibility)\n      if (typeof encoding === 'function') {\n        encoding();\n      } else if (typeof callback === 'function') {\n        callback();\n      }\n      return true;\n    };\n\n    try {\n      yargsInstance = createYargsConfig(yargs());\n      argv = await yargsInstance.parse(rawArgs);\n    } finally {\n      // Always restore stderr.write\n      process.stderr.write = originalStderrWrite;\n\n      // In verbose mode, show what was captured from stderr (for debugging)\n      if (global.verboseMode && stderrBuffer.length > 0) {\n        const captured = stderrBuffer.join('');\n        if (captured.trim()) {\n          console.error('[Suppressed yargs stderr]:', captured);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  } catch (error) {\n    // Yargs throws errors for validation issues\n    // If the error is about unknown arguments (strict mode), enhance it with suggestions\n    // Check if this error has already been enhanced to avoid re-processing\n    if (error.message && /Unknown argument/.test(error.message) && !error._enhanced) {\n      try {\n        // Enhance the error message with helpful suggestions\n        // Use the yargsInstance we already created, or create a new one if needed\n        const yargsWithConfig = yargsInstance || createYargsConfig(yargs());\n        const enhancedMessage = enhanceErrorMessage(error.message, yargsWithConfig);\n        const enhancedError = new Error(enhancedMessage);\n        enhancedError.name = error.name;\n        enhancedError._enhanced = true; // Mark as enhanced to prevent re-processing\n        throw enhancedError;\n      } catch (enhanceErr) {\n        // If enhancing fails, just throw the original error\n        if (global.verboseMode) {\n          console.error('[VERBOSE] Failed to enhance error message:', enhanceErr.message);\n        }\n        // If the enhance error itself is already enhanced, throw it\n        if (enhanceErr._enhanced) {\n          throw enhanceErr;\n        }\n        throw error;\n      }\n    }\n    // For other validation errors, show a warning in verbose mode\n    if (error.message && global.verboseMode) {\n      console.error('Yargs parsing warning:', error.message);\n    }\n    // Try to get the argv even with the error\n    argv = error.argv || {};\n  }\n\n  // Post-processing: Fix model default for opencode and codex tools\n  // Yargs doesn't properly handle dynamic defaults based on other arguments,\n  // so we need to handle this manually after parsing\n  const modelExplicitlyProvided = rawArgs.includes('--model') || rawArgs.includes('-m') || rawArgs.includes('--worker-model');\n  const fallbackModelExplicitlyProvided = rawArgs.includes('--fallback-model');\n  const planModelExplicitlyProvided = rawArgs.includes('--plan-model');\n\n  // --plan flag expansion (Issue #1223)\n  // When --plan is set, it acts as a shortcut for --plan-model opus --worker-model sonnet\n  // Explicit --plan-model and --model/--worker-model values take precedence\n  if (argv && argv.plan) {\n    if (!planModelExplicitlyProvided) {\n      argv.planModel = 'opus';\n    }\n    if (!modelExplicitlyProvided) {\n      argv.model = 'sonnet';\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Normalize alias flags: legacy --skip-tool-check and --skip-claude-check behave like --skip-tool-connection-check\n  if (argv) {\n    // Support deprecated flags\n    if (argv.skipToolCheck || argv.skipClaudeCheck) {\n      argv.skipToolConnectionCheck = true;\n    }\n    // Support negated deprecated flag: --no-tool-check becomes --no-tool-connection-check\n    if (argv.toolCheck === false) {\n      argv.toolConnectionCheck = false;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // --finalize normalization\n  // Issue #1383: When finalize is enabled (as boolean or number), normalize to iteration count\n  // NOTE: promptEnsureAllRequirementsAreMet is NOT set here — it is only enabled during\n  // the finalize cycle iterations themselves (not the first regular worker model run)\n  if (argv && argv.finalize) {\n    // Normalize: if passed as boolean true (flag without value), treat as 1 iteration\n    if (argv.finalize === true) {\n      argv.finalize = 1;\n    }\n  }\n\n  // --working-session-live-progress normalization\n  // When passed as --working-session-live-progress (no value), yargs gives true for string type\n  // Normalize: true → \"comment\", validate known values\n  if (argv && argv.workingSessionLiveProgress) {\n    const val = argv.workingSessionLiveProgress;\n    if (val === true || val === 'true') {\n      argv.workingSessionLiveProgress = 'comment';\n    } else if (typeof val === 'string' && !['comment', 'pr'].includes(val.toLowerCase())) {\n      throw new Error(`Invalid --working-session-live-progress value: \"${val}\". // MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT: Timeout in milliseconds for MCP tool execution\n  // Default: 900000ms (15 minutes) to accommodate long-running Playwright operations\n  // Set via MCP_TIMEOUT/MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const normalizedModel = model.toLowerCase();\n  // Check for explicit opus-4-6 or later versions, or opusplan (Issue #1223)\n  // Note: The 'opus' alias now maps to Opus 4.7 (Issue #1620), so we also check for the alias directly\n  // opusplan uses Opus for planning, so it should get Opus-level settings\n  return normalizedModel === 'opus' || normalizedModel === 'opusplan' || normalizedModel.includes('opus-4-6') || normalizedModel.includes('opus-4-7') || normalizedModel.includes('opus-5');\n};\n\nconst isOpus47 = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const normalizedModel = model.toLowerCase();\n  // 'opus' alias now maps to Opus 4.7 (Issue #1620)\n  // opusplan uses Opus for planning, so it gets Opus-level settings\n  return normalizedModel === 'opus' || normalizedModel === 'opusplan' || normalizedModel.includes('opus-4-7');\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if a model is Opus 4.7 or later (Issue #1620)\n * These models use Opus 4.7+ adaptive thinking const normalizedModel = model.toLowerCase();\n  return isOpus47(model) || normalizedModel.includes('opus-5');\n};\n\nconst isOpus45 = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const m = model.toLowerCase();\n  return m === 'opus-4-5' || m.includes('opus-4-5');\n};\n\nconst isOpus46 = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const m = model.toLowerCase();\n  return m === 'opus-4-6' || m.includes('opus-4-6');\n};\n\nconst isSonnet46OrLater = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const m = model.toLowerCase();\n  return m === 'sonnet' || m === 'sonnet-4-6' || supportsXHighEffortLevel = model => isOpus47(model);\n\n/**\n * Check if a model supports the max effort level.\n * Official docs list max for Claude Mythos Preview, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet isOpus47OrLater(model) || isOpus46(model) || isSonnet46OrLater(model);\n\n/**\n * Get the max output tokens for a specific model (Issue #1221)\n * @param {string} model - The model name or ID\n * return DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET;\n};\n\n/**\n * Get thinking level token values calculated from max budget\n * Values are evenly distributed: off=0, low=max/4, medium=max/2, high=max*3/4, max=max\n * @param {number} maxBudget - Maximum thinking budget (default: 31999)\n * @returns {Object} Mapping of thinking levels to token values\n */\nexport const getThinkingLevelToTokens = (maxBudget = DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET) => ({\n  off: 0,\n  low: Math.floor(maxBudget / 4), // ~8000 for default 31999\n  medium: Math.floor(maxBudget / 2), // ~16000 for default 31999\n  high: Math.floor((maxBudget * 3) / 4), // ~24000 for default 31999\n  xhigh: maxBudget, // same as max when represented as MAX_THINKING_TOKENS\n  max: maxBudget, // 31999 by default\n});\n\n// Default thinking level to tokens mapping (using default max budget)\nexport const thinkingLevelToTokens = getThinkingLevelToTokens(DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET);\n\n/**\n * Get tokens to thinking level mapping converts tokens to thinking level\n */\nexport const getTokensToThinkingLevel = (maxBudget = DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET) => {\n  const levels = getThinkingLevelToTokens(maxBudget);\n  // Calculate midpoints between levels for range determination\n  const lowMediumMidpoint = Math.floor((levels.low + levels.medium) / 2);\n  const mediumHighMidpoint = Math.floor((levels.medium + levels.high) / 2);\n  const highMaxMidpoint = Math.floor((levels.high + levels.max) / 2);\n\n  return tokens => {\n    if (tokens === 0) return 'off';\n    if (tokens <= lowMediumMidpoint) return 'low';\n    if (tokens <= mediumHighMidpoint) return 'medium';\n    if (tokens <= highMaxMidpoint) return 'high';\n    return 'max';\n  };\n};\n\n// Default tokens to thinking level function (using default max }\n\n  const thinkLevel = getTokensToThinkingLevel(maxBudget)(thinkingBudget);\n  return thinkLevelToEffortLevel(thinkLevel, options);\n};\n\n// Check if a version supports thinking budget (>= minimum or later (Issue #1221, updated in Issue #1238)\n * @param {string} model - The model name or ID\n * @returns {boolean} True if the model is Opus 4.6 or later\n */\nexport const isOpus46OrLater = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const normalizedModel = model.toLowerCase();\n  // Check for explicit opus-4-6 or later versions, or opusplan (Issue #1223)\n  // Note: The 'opus' alias now maps to Opus 4.7 (Issue #1620), so we also check for the alias directly\n  // opusplan uses Opus for planning, so it should get Opus-level settings\n  return normalizedModel === 'opus' || normalizedModel === 'opusplan' || normalizedModel.includes('opus-4-6') || normalizedModel.includes('opus-4-7') || normalizedModel.includes('opus-5');\n};\n\nconst isOpus47 = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const normalizedModel = model.toLowerCase();\n  // 'opus' alias now maps to Opus 4.7 (Issue #1620)\n  // opusplan uses Opus for planning, so it gets Opus-level settings\n  return normalizedModel === 'opus' || normalizedModel === 'opusplan' || normalizedModel.includes('opus-4-7');\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if a model is Opus 4.7 or later (Issue #1620)\n * These models use Opus 4.7+ adaptive thinking const normalizedModel = model.toLowerCase();\n  return isOpus47(model) || normalizedModel.includes('opus-5');\n};\n\nconst isOpus45 = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const m = model.toLowerCase();\n  return m === 'opus-4-5' || m.includes('opus-4-5');\n};\n\nconst isOpus46 = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const m = model.toLowerCase();\n  return m === 'opus-4-6' || m.includes('opus-4-6');\n};\n\nconst isSonnet46OrLater = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  const m = model.toLowerCase();\n  return m === 'sonnet' || m === 'sonnet-4-6' || m.includes('sonnet-4-6') || m.includes('sonnet-5');\n};\n\nconst isMythosPreview = model => {\n  if (!model) return false;\n  return model.toLowerCase().includes('mythos');\n};\n\n/**\n * Check if a isOpus47OrLater(model) || isOpus46(model) || isSonnet46OrLater(model);\n\n/**\n * Get the max output tokens for a specific model (Issue #1221)\n * @param {string} model - The model name or ID\n * return DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET;\n};\n\n/**\n * Get thinking level token values calculated from max budget\n * Values are evenly distributed: off=0, low=max/4, medium=max/2, high=max*3/4, max=max\n * @param {number} maxBudget - Maximum thinking budget (default: 31999)\n * @returns {Object} Mapping of thinking levels to token values\n */\nexport const getThinkingLevelToTokens = (maxBudget = DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET) => ({\n  off: 0,\n  low: Math.floor(maxBudget / 4), // ~8000 for default 31999\n  medium: Math.floor(maxBudget / 2), // ~16000 for default 31999\n  high: Math.floor((maxBudget * 3) / 4), // ~24000 for default 31999\n  xhigh: maxBudget, // same as max when represented as MAX_THINKING_TOKENS\n  max: maxBudget, // 31999 by default\n});\n\n// Default thinking level to tokens mapping (using default max budget)\nexport const thinkingLevelToTokens = getThinkingLevelToTokens(DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET);\n\n/**\n * Get tokens to thinking level mapping function with configurable max budget\n * Uses midpoint ranges to determine the level\n * @param {number} maxBudget - Maximum thinking budget (default: 31999)\n * @returns {Function} Function that converts tokens to thinking level\n */\nexport const getTokensToThinkingLevel = (maxBudget = DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET) => {\n  const levels = getThinkingLevelToTokens(maxBudget);\n  // Calculate midpoints between levels for range determination\n  const lowMediumMidpoint = Math.floor((levels.low + levels.medium) / 2);\n  const mediumHighMidpoint = Math.floor((levels.medium + levels.high) / 2);\n  const highMaxMidpoint = Math.floor((levels.high + levels.max) / 2);\n\n  return tokens => {\n    if (tokens === 0) return 'off';\n    if (tokens <= lowMediumMidpoint) return 'low';\n    if (tokens <= mediumHighMidpoint) return 'medium';\n    if (tokens <= highMaxMidpoint) return 'high';\n    return 'max';\n  };\n};\n\n// Default tokens to thinking level function (using default max budget)\nexport const tokensToThinkingLevel = getTokensToThinkingLevel(DEFAULT_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET);\n\n/**\n * Valid effort levels for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 (Issue #1238, Issue #1620)\n * These }\n\n  const thinkLevel = getTokensToThinkingLevel(maxBudget)(thinkingBudget);\n  return thinkLevelToEffortLevel(thinkLevel, options);\n};\n\n// Check if a version supports thinking budget (>= minimum config = config\n    .option('model', {\n      type: 'string',\n      description: buildModelOptionDescription(),\n      alias: ['m', 'worker-model'],\n      default: currentParsedArgs => {\n        // Dynamic default based on tool selection (Issue #1473: centralized in models/index.mjs)\n        return defaultModels[currentParsedArgs?.tool] || defaultModels.claude;\n      },\n    })\n    .parserConfiguration({\n      'boolean-negation': true,\n    })\n    // Use yargs built-in strict mode to reject unrecognized options\n    // This prevents issues like #453 and #482 where unknown options are silently ignored\n    .strict()\n    .help('h')\n    .alias('h', 'help');\n\n  return config;\n};\n\n// Parse command line arguments - now needs yargs and hideBin passed in\nexport const model\" which yargs silently treats as positional arguments\n  const malformedResult = detectMalformedFlags(rawArgs);\n  if (malformedResult.malformed.length > 0) {\n    const error = new Error(malformedResult.errors.join('\\n'));\n    error.name = 'MalformedArgumentError';\n    throw error;\n  }\n\n  // Use .parse() instead of .argv to ensure .strict() mode works correctly\n  // When you call yargs(args) and use .argv, strict mode doesn't trigger\n  // See: https://github.com/yargs/yargs/issues - .strict() only works with .parse()\n\n  let argv;\n  let yargsInstance;\n  try {\n    // Suppress stderr output from yargs during parsing to prevent validation errors from appearing\n    // This prevents \"YError: Not enough arguments\" from polluting stderr (issue #583)\n    // Save the original stderr.write\n    const originalStderrWrite = process.stderr.write;\n    const stderrBuffer = [];\n\n    // Temporarily override stderr.write to capture output\n    process.stderr.write = function (chunk, encoding, callback) {\n      stderrBuffer.push(chunk.toString());\n      // Call the callback if provided (for compatibility)\n      if (typeof encoding === 'function') {\n        encoding();\n      } else if (typeof callback === 'function') {\n        callback();\n      }\n      return true;\n    };\n\n    try {\n      yargsInstance = createYargsConfig(yargs());\n      argv = await yargsInstance.parse(rawArgs);\n    } finally {\n      // Always restore stderr.write\n      process.stderr.write = originalStderrWrite;\n\n      // In verbose mode, show what was captured from stderr (for debugging)\n      if (global.verboseMode && stderrBuffer.length > 0) {\n        const captured = stderrBuffer.join('');\n        if (captured.trim()) {\n          console.error('[Suppressed yargs stderr]:', captured);\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  } catch (error) {\n    // Yargs throws errors for validation issues\n    // If the error is about unknown arguments (strict mode), enhance it with suggestions\n    // Check if this error has already been enhanced to avoid re-processing\n    if (error.message && /Unknown argument/.test(error.message) && !error._enhanced) {\n      try {\n        // Enhance the error message with helpful suggestions\n        // Use the yargsInstance we already created, or create a new one if needed\n        const yargsWithConfig = yargsInstance || createYargsConfig(yargs());\n        const enhancedMessage = enhanceErrorMessage(error.message, yargsWithConfig);\n        const enhancedError = new Error(enhancedMessage);\n        enhancedError.name = error.name;\n        enhancedError._enhanced = true; // Mark as enhanced to prevent re-processing\n        throw enhancedError;\n      } catch Cache TTL Configurations\n\nThese settings control how long API responses are cached before making a new request.\n\n| Environment Variable               | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                       |\n| ---------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `HIVE_MIND_API_CACHE_TTL_MS`       | 180000  | General API cache TTL in ms (3 minutes). Used for GitHub API.                                                                                                     |\n| `HIVE_MIND_USAGE_API_CACHE_TTL_MS` | 600000  | Claude Usage API cache TTL in ms (10 minutes). **Important:** The Claude Usage API has stricter rate limiting. Calling it more frequently may return null values. |\n| `HIVE_MIND_SYSTEM_CACHE_TTL_MS`    | 120000  | System metrics cache TTL in ms (2 minutes). Used for RAM, CPU, and disk space.                                                                                    |\n\n**Note:** The Claude Usage API (`/api/oauth/usage`) is rate-limited more strictly than other APIs. If you experience `null` values in the `/limits` command output, the API call frequency may be too high. The default 10-minute TTL is designed to avoid this issue. See [Issue #1074](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1074) for details.\n\n### 5.2. Claude Code CLI Configurations\n\nThese settings control Claude Code CLI behavior, including output limits and MCP timeouts.\n\n| Environment Variable                    | Default | Description                                                                                           |\n| --------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`         | 64000   | Maximum output tokens for Claude Code CLI responses (also: `HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`) |\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_OPUS_46` | 128000  | Maximum output tokens for Opus 4.6+ (also: `HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_OPUS_46`)         |\n| `MCP_TIMEOUT`                           | 900000  | MCP server startup timeout in ms (15 min) (also: `HIVE_MIND_MCP_TIMEOUT`)                             |\n| `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`                      | 900000  | MCP tool execution timeout in ms (15 min) (also: `HIVE_MIND_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`)                        |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET_OPUS_46` | 31999   | Default max thinking budget for Opus 4.6+ models                                                      |\n\n**Note:** Claude models support different max output tokens: Opus 4.6 (the default `opus` alias) supports 128K tokens, while Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, and Haiku 4.5 support 64K tokens. The MCP timeouts (15 minutes by default) accommodate long-running Playwright operations. See [Issue #1076](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1076) and [Issue #1066](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1066) for details.\n\n### 6. Playwright MCP\n\nPlaywright MCP (Model Context Protocol) provides browser automation capabilities for Claude Code and Codex, enabling web scraping, UI testing, and interaction with dynamic web pages.\n\n#### Installation\n\n```bash\n# Recommended: Install with memory-safe settings (for servers and Docker)\nclaude mcp add playwright -s user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless --no-sandbox --timeout-action=600000 --viewport-size 1920x1080\ncodex mcp add playwright -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless --no-sandbox --timeout-action=600000 --viewport-size 1920x1080\n\n# Minimal installation (for local development)\nclaude mcp add playwright -s user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless\ncodex mcp add playwright -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless\n```\n\n#### Command-Line Arguments\n\n| Argument                 | Description                                    | Memory Impact                              |\n| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |\n| `--isolated`             | Ephemeral browser contexts (MOST IMPORTANT)    | **HIGH** - Prevents process accumulation   |\n| `--headless`             | Run browser in headless mode                   | **MEDIUM** - Reduces UI memory overhead    |\n| `--browser <type>`       | Browser: chromium, firefox, webkit, msedge     | **VARIES** - WebKit often uses less memory |\n| `--no-sandbox`           | Disable sandbox (controlled environments only) | **LOW** - Reduces memory slightly          |\n| `--timeout-action <ms>`  | Timeout for actions (default: 5000)            | **N/A** - Prevents hung processes          |\n| `--viewport-size <size>` | Set viewport dimensions (e.g., \"1280x720\")     | **LOW** - Affects rendering memory         |\n| `--storage-state <path>` | Load auth state without full profile           | **MEDIUM** - Auth without profile bloat    |\n\n#### Scope Options\n\nClaude Code and Codex do not share MCP registration automatically. Register Playwright MCP in each CLI you expect to use. A working Claude configuration does not make `codex mcp list` show the same server.\n\n| Scope     | Description                     | Config Location                     |\n| --------- | ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |\n| `local`   | Current directory only          | `~/.claude.json` (project-specific) |\n| `project` | Team-shared via version control | `.mcp.json` (project root)          |\n| `user`    | Available globally              | `~/.claude.json` (user section)     |\n\n#### JSON Configuration\n\nClaude Code example (`~/.claude.json`):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"playwright\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"@playwright/mcp@latest\", \"--isolated\", \"--headless\", \"--no-sandbox\", \"--timeout-action=600000\", \"--viewport-size\", \"1920x1080\"],\n      \"env\": {\n        \"PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH\": \"/opt/playwright/browsers\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nCodex stores MCP configuration separately. Use the Codex CLI to inspect or register its own Playwright entry:\n\n```bash\n# List configured MCP servers\ncodex mcp list\n\n# Add server\ncodex mcp add playwright -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless --no-sandbox --timeout-action=600000 --viewport-size 1920x1080\n\n# Remove server\ncodex mcp remove playwright\n```\n\n#### MCP Commands\n\n```bash\n# List configured MCP servers\nclaude mcp list\ncodex mcp list\n\n# Get server details\nclaude mcp get playwright\n\n# Remove server\nclaude mcp remove playwright\ncodex mcp remove playwright\n```\n\n#### Best Practices\n\n1. **Always use `--isolated` mode** - Prevents Chrome process accumulation and memory leaks\n2. **Pin to a specific version** - Use `@playwright/mcp@0.0.49` instead of `@latest` for stability\n3. **Use `--headless` for servers** - Reduces memory overhead in CI/CD and production environments\n4. **Restart Claude Code periodically** - For long-running sessions to clear accumulated browser resources\n\nFor comprehensive configuration options, troubleshooting, and advanced use cases, see the detailed guide:\n[Playwright MCP Configuration Guide](./case-studies/issue-837-playwright-mcp-chrome-leak/04-CLAUDE-PLAYWRIGHT-MCP-CONFIGURATION.md)\n\n---\n\n## Command-Line Options\n\n### solve Options\n\n```bash\nsolve <issue-url> [options]\n```\n\n| Option                                                           | Alias | Type    | Default             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `--model`                                                        | `-m`  | string  | depends on `--tool` | Model to use. GitHub API 限制\n\n| 环境变量                               | 默认值   | 描述                                |\n| -------------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------- |\n| `HIVE_MIND_GITHUB_BUFFER_MAX_SIZE`     | 10485760 | GitHub 操作的最大缓冲区大小（10MB） |\n\n### 4. 系统资源限制\n\n| 环境变量                         | 默认值 | 描述                   |\n| -------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------- |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MIN_DISK_SPACE_MB`    | 2048   | 最小所需磁盘空间（MB） |\n| `HIVE_MIND_DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE_KB` | 16     | 默认内存页大小（KB）   |\n\n### 5. 重试配置\n\n| 环境变量                               | 默认值 | 描述                        |\n| -------------------------------------- | ------ | --------------------------- |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MAX_FORK_RETRIES`           | 5      | 最大 Fork 创建重试次数      |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MAX_VERIFY_RETRIES`         | 5      | 最大验证重试次数            |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MAX_API_RETRIES`            | 3      | 最大 API 调用重试次数       |\n| `HIVE_MIND_RETRY_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER`   | 2      | 重试退避乘数                |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MAX_503_RETRIES`            | 3      | 最大 503 错误重试次数       |\n| `HIVE_MIND_INITIAL_503_RETRY_DELAY_MS` | 300000 | 初始 503 重试延迟（5 分钟） |\n\n### 5.1. 缓存 TTL 配置\n\n这些设置控制 API 响应被缓存多长时间，超过该时间后将发起新请求。\n\n| 环境变量                           | 默认值 | 描述                                                                                                                     |\n| ---------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| `HIVE_MIND_API_CACHE_TTL_MS`       | 180000 | 通用 API 缓存 TTL（毫秒，3 分钟）。用于 GitHub API。                                                                     |\n| `HIVE_MIND_USAGE_API_CACHE_TTL_MS` | 600000 | Claude 用量 API 缓存 TTL（毫秒，10 分钟）。**重要：** Claude 用量 API 有更严格的速率限制。调用频率过高可能返回 null 值。 |\n| `HIVE_MIND_SYSTEM_CACHE_TTL_MS`    | 120000 | 系统指标缓存 TTL（毫秒，2 分钟）。用于 RAM、CPU 和磁盘空间。                                                             |\n\n**注意：** Claude 用量 API（`/api/oauth/usage`）的速率限制比其他 API 更严格。如果您在 `/limits` 命令输出中遇到 `null` 值，可能是 API 调用频率过高。默认的 10 分钟 TTL 旨在避免此问题。详情请参阅 [Issue #1074](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1074)。\n\n### 5.2. Claude Code CLI 配置\n\n这些设置控制 Claude Code CLI 的行为，包括输出限制和 MCP 超时。\n\n| 环境变量                                | 默认值 | 描述                                                                                           |\n| --------------------------------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`         | 64000  | Claude Code CLI 响应的最大输出 token 数（也可使用：`HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`） |\n| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_OPUS_46` | 128000 | Opus 4.6+ 的最大输出 token 数（也可使用：`HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS_OPUS_46`）   |\n| `MCP_TIMEOUT`                           | 900000 | MCP 服务器启动超时（毫秒，15 分钟）（也可使用：`HIVE_MIND_MCP_TIMEOUT`）                       |\n| `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`                      | 900000 | MCP 工具执行超时（毫秒，15 分钟）（也可使用：`HIVE_MIND_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`）                    |\n| `HIVE_MIND_MAX_THINKING_BUDGET_OPUS_46` | 31999  | Opus 4.6+ 模型的默认最大思考预算                                                               |\n\n**注意：** Claude 模型支持不同的最大输出 token 数：Opus 4.6（默认 `opus` 别名）支持 128K token，而 Sonnet 4.5、Opus 4.5 和 Haiku 4.5 支持 64K token。MCP 超时时间（默认 15 分钟）可容纳长时间运行的 Playwright 操作。详情请参阅 [Issue #1076](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1076) 和 [Issue #1066](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1066)。\n\n### 6. Playwright MCP\n\nPlaywright MCP（模型上下文协议）为 Claude Code 提供浏览器自动化功能，支持网页抓取、UI 测试以及与动态网页的交互。\n\n#### 安装\n\n```bash\n# 推荐：使用内存安全设置安装（适用于服务器和 Docker）\nclaude mcp add playwright -s user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless --no-sandbox --timeout-action=600000 --viewport-size 1920x1080\n\n# 最简安装（适用于本地开发）\nclaude mcp add playwright -s user -- npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest --isolated --headless\n```\n\n#### 命令行参数\n\n| 参数                     | 描述                                      | 内存影响                           |\n| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |\n| `--isolated`             | 临时浏览器上下文（最重要）                | **高** - 防止进程积累              |\n| `--headless`             | 以无头模式运行浏览器                      | **中** - 减少 UI 内存开销          |\n| `--browser <type>`       | 浏览器：chromium、firefox、webkit、msedge | **不一** - WebKit 通常使用更少内存 |\n| `--no-sandbox`           | 禁用沙盒（仅限受控环境）                  | **低** - 稍微减少内存              |\n| `--timeout-action <ms>`  | 操作超时（默认：5000）                    | **不适用** - 防止进程挂起          |\n| `--viewport-size <size>` | 设置视口尺寸（例如 \"1280x720\"）           | **低** - 影响渲染内存              |\n| `--storage-state <path>` | 加载认证状态而无需完整配置文件            | **中** - 无配置文件膨胀的认证      |\n\n#### 作用域选项\n\n| 作用域    | 描述                   | 配置位置                     |\n| --------- | ---------------------- | ---------------------------- |\n| `local`   | 仅限当前目录           | `~/.claude.json`（项目特定） |\n| `project` | 通过版本控制共享给团队 | `.mcp.json`（项目根目录）    |\n| `user`    | 全局可用               | `~/.claude.json`（用户部分） |\n\n#### JSON 配置\n\n在 `~/.claude.json` 中直接配置：\n\n```json\n{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"playwright\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"@playwright/mcp@latest\", \"--isolated\", \"--headless\", \"--no-sandbox\", \"--timeout-action=600000\", \"--viewport-size\", \"1920x1080\"],\n      \"env\": {\n        \"PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH\": \"/opt/playwright/browsers\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n#### MCP 命令\n\n```bash\n# 列出已配置的 MCP 服务器\nclaude mcp list\n\n# 获取服务器详情\nclaude mcp get playwright\n\n# 移除服务器\nclaude mcp remove playwright\n```\n\n#### 最佳实践\n\n1. **始终使用 `--isolated` 模式** - 防止 Chrome 进程积累和内存泄漏\n2. **固定到特定版本** - 使用 `@playwright/mcp@0.0.49` 而非 `@latest` 以确保稳定性\n3. **在服务器上使用 `--headless`** - 减少 CI/CD 和生产环境中的内存开销\n4. **定期重启 Claude Code** - 对于长时间运行的会话，以清除积累的浏览器资源\n\n如需完整的配置选项、故障排除和高级使用场景，请参阅详细指南：\n[Playwright MCP 配置指南](./case-studies/issue-837-playwright-mcp-chrome-leak/04-CLAUDE-PLAYWRIGHT-MCP-CONFIGURATION.md)\n\n---\n\n## 命令行选项\n\n### solve 选项\n\n```bash\nsolve <issue-url> [options]\n```\n\n| 选项 使用自定义超时运行\nHIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120 HIVE_MIND_RETRY_BASE_DELAY_MS=10000 hive https://github.com/owner/repo\n\n# 使用增加的限制运行\nHIVE_MIND_GITHUB_FILE_MAX_SIZE=52428800 https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/456\n```\n\n### 配置文件（可选）\n\n您可以在项目根目录创建 `.env` 文件：\n\n```bash\n# .env 文件\nHIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=90\nHIVE_MIND_GITHUB_API_DELAY_MS=3000\nHIVE_MIND_AUTO_CONTINUE_AGE_HOURS=36\nHIVE_MIND_TEMP_DIR=/opt/hive-mind/tmp\nHIVE_MIND_SENTRY_DSN=your-custom-sentry-dsn\n```\n\n然后在运行前加载它：\n\n```bash\nsource .env\nhive https://github.com/owner/repo\n```\n\n### 开发者用法\n\n```javascript\nimport { timeouts, githubLimits, sentry } from './config.lib.mjs';\n\n// 使用配置值\nconst timeout = timeouts.claudeCli;\nconst
